title: Decimal Exact-Fill Minimum Items
prompt:
Implement `min_exact_items(durations, target) -> int`. Each duration and the target has at most one decimal place. Select durations with unlimited reuse and return the fewest selections whose sum is exactly `target`. Return `0` when no exact selection exists; `target == 0` also returns `0`.

Do not use binary floating-point equality for this task. Convert every value to integer tenths before computing the result. Duplicate duration values do not change what totals are reachable, and one duration may be selected more than once. Assume every duration is positive and the target is nonnegative.

Use dynamic programming where the state for each scaled total stores its best known item count. Aim for O(target_in_tenths * len(durations)) time and O(target_in_tenths) space.

example.reasoning: Two 2.5 durations and one 1.5 duration make 6.5 with three selections.
